summary: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) was an Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders). He served at the Archaeological Survey of India and was General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI.

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Elphinstone College under Ramachandra Balkrishna, he later served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and as an examiner in Marathi and Law at Mumbai University.

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar of Indology and history who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, serving as professor (attested 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and history. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach.

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Institute, headed Sanskrit at Vikram University, served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, and chaired the ICPR.

Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who completed his MA under Karin Preisendanz and studied with Chlodwig H. Werba and Roque Mesquita. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at the University of Vienna.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) worked in Indology and history. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Kalyanov (1908–2001) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Institute for Philosophy, Literature and History in Leningrad and under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from circa 1938 to 2001.

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and historian. After studying at Moscow Imperial University and the Lazarev Institute, he held positions at INALCO (circa 1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (circa 1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973) works in Buddhist, religious, and historical studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University, he lectured at Kyung Hee University before joining the University of Oslo, where he became a professor in 2006.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich and LIRI, and teaches at Leipzig, Bern, and Hamburg.

Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) is a historian of Southeast Asia educated at Kiel and Chiang Mai. He held posts at Passau, Münster, and the National University of Laos, before becoming Chair of Thai language and culture at Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz (born 1956) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and with Anagarika Govinda. He held academic posts at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and Luxembourg universities.
W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) was an anthropologist and medical scholar who studied at London and St Bartholomew's. He held medical posts, taught at Cambridge and UCL, became a Fellow at St John's, and presided over the Anthropological Society.

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught at Johns Hopkins and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1926 to 1966.
W. Pachow (born 1918) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and held a teaching and research post at Visva-Bharati University.

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religious, Indological, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1964. He has taught courses at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard Divinity School in 1998.

Wai Lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and Chairperson in Cultural and Religious Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).
